They name their lands after themselves. But man, despite his riches, doesn't endure. He is like the animals that perish.” (web:Ps.49.11, web:Ps.49.12). The refrain line at 49:12 recurs at 49:20 with a three-word-slot delta rather than a single substitution: oshb:Ps.49.21 drops the vav-conjunctive that opens וְאָדָ֣ם at oshb:Ps.49.13, and swaps both the negator and the verb of the medial clause, בַּל יָלִ֑ין ('does not lodge') becoming וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין ('does not understand') — a word-level comparison across the 2-verse refrain pair (sweep: 2 verses compared), so the pair reads as a near-repeated refrain rather than a byte-identical one, and it is this recurring line, not the intervening Selahs (which fall in the next span), that closes this movement.

A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish.” (web:Ps.49.19, web:Ps.49.20), which repeats 49:12's frame with a three-word-slot delta — the opening vav-conjunctive dropped and both the negator and verb of the medial clause swapped — rather than one substituted verb (see the seam at 49:12|49:13).
